all.src: Trend filter: spot > 50-day SMA AND 50-day SMA > 200-day SMA; underlying must not have declined more than 15% in the last 20 sessions.
IV rank < 35 at the time of the LEAPS purchase (the long leg is your biggest vega exposure).
LEAPS: delta 0.80-0.90, DTE >= 180 (270-730 preferred), extrinsic <= 10% of premium.
LEAPS: delta 0.80-0.90, DTE >= 180 (270-730 preferred), extrinsic <= 10% of premium.

management.src: Close the short call at 50-75% of the credit received, then immediately sell the next cycle's 0.20-0.30 delta call at 21-45 DTE. This roll cadence is the income engine.

If the short call's |delta| exceeds 0.50, roll it up and out for a NET CREDIT only, and only to a strike still >= long strike + remaining net debit. If no credit roll satisfies that, close the short and let the LEAPS run naked-long (which is allowed and has no assignment risk) until a valid strike appears.

exits.src: LEAPS: delta 0.80-0.90, DTE >= 180 (270-730 preferred), extrinsic <= 10% of premium.
Close or roll the short call by 14:30 ET on its expiration day, unconditionally. A PMCC short call that expires ITM means -100 shares delivered on Monday.
Close the short call immediately if its extrinsic value <= $0.05/share or |delta| >= 0.90.

Close the short call before the close of the session preceding ex-dividend whenever its extrinsic value < the declared dividend per share. This is the #1 cause of PMCC assignment, and it typically happens when the stock has rallied through the short strike.
Close the LEAPS no later than 90 DTE, and always after the short call has been bought back.
